intervention: Dissolvable oral nicotine tablet (mint flavour) at five nicotine contents — 0 mg, 0.5 mg, 1.0 mg, 1.5 mg, 2.0 mg — used for approximately 10 minutes, double-blind crossover. This is a true dose-response design, which is unusual and makes it more informative than a single-dose comparison.
population: Adults 19-60, healthy-volunteers flag true, condition listed as 'Attention'. Participants are current non-daily users of nicotine pouches (past 30-day use) who express no desire to quit; excluded if using NRT or cessation medication, if urine cotinine exceeds 500 ng/mL, or if exhaled CO is at least 10 ppm. My judgement: healthy adults, NOT a patient group — but explicitly nicotine-experienced rather than nicotine-naive, which matters because acute nicotine effects in users can partly reflect relief of mild abstinence rather than net enhancement.
primary_cognitive_outcome: Change in attentional performance 15 minutes after the start of product use, assessed with the Conners Continuous Performance Test (CPT). Secondary outcome repeats the CPT at 2 hours to probe sustained effects.
